source_steps.text: By H003 and H004, h y^0v=λv. For the h-identity, assume the induction hypothesis L1: hy^d v=(λ-2d)y^dv. Then hy^(d+1)v=(yh-2y)y^dv=(λ-2d-2)y^(d+1)v. Discharging L1 and using induction proves the h-identity for every d≥0. Also xyv=(yx+h)v=λv. For the x-identity, at an arbitrary d≥1 assume L2: xy^dv=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v. The just proved h-identity gives xy^(d+1)v=(yx+h)y^dv=[d(λ-d+1)+λ-2d]y^dv=(d+1)(λ-d)y^dv. Discharging L2 and inducting from d=1 proves the x-identity. The d=0 x-value is xv=0. These are identities of complex vectors; no reduction of weights has occurred.

H001 implies n>0 and |I|=λ+1=n. Iterating F001 gives x^i y^iv=i!·λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v for i∈I. Every factor in this product is nonzero over C when i≥1, and the i=0 product is one; H004 therefore gives e_i≠0. Also he_i=(λ-2i)e_i by F001. The eigenvalues λ-2i are pairwise distinct over C. Assume L3: Σ_{i∈I}α_i e_i=0. For arbitrary j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id_V). All terms except the j-th vanish, leaving α_j·(∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k-j))e_j=0. Its vector and scalar product are nonzero (empty product one), so α_j=0. Discharge L3: every relation is trivial. There are n independent vectors and dim_C V=n by H002, hence they form a basis.

F001 at d=λ+1 gives h y^(λ+1)v=(-λ-2)y^(λ+1)v. Expanding this vector in the basis F002, the equation says that its coefficient at every e_i is killed by (λ-2i)-(-λ-2)=2(λ+1-i), nonzero over C for i∈I. Thus y^(λ+1)v=0; equivalently a nonzero vector of this eigenvalue would contradict the basis spectrum. Applying further powers of y gives y^dv=0 for all d>λ.

For i∈I the definitions and F001 give xe_0=0 and xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) for i≥1. They also give ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 by F003, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. Iterating these formulas r times and dividing by r! yields X_r e_i=[(λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!]e_(i-r)=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) for r≤i, and Y_r e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) for i+r≤λ. The products are empty when r=0. Otherwise the x-string reaches e_0 and is killed, or the y-string passes e_λ and is killed, so the remaining cases give zero. These coefficients are integers by the usual finite binomial formula. Together with F001–F003 this proves every clause of the output.

Choose the basis m from H005. It has n members because it and the N001 basis are both complex bases of V. The tensors of its members with 1 give an R-basis of R⊗_Z M: the integer coordinate maps extend to inverse R-coordinate maps, exhibiting the isomorphism with R^n. Under μ a tensor has these same coordinates as a complex linear combination of the members of m, so complex independence makes μ injective. Its image contains M and therefore spans V over C. Admissibility in H005 gives X_r M,Y_r M⊆M for every r≥0. Extending each operator R-linearly preserves M_R and commutes with μ. From now on identify M_R with its image.

Define Q=Y_λ X_λ. On the basis N001, X_λ kills every e_k except e_λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Hence Q=E_(λλ), and X_(λ-i)Q=E_(iλ), again with coefficient binom(λ-i,λ-i)=1. Also QY_(λ-j)=binom(λ,j)E_(λj): an input index below j lands below e_λ and is killed by Q; an input above j passes the end of the lowering string; the input e_j has coefficient binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). Since 0≤j≤λ

For arbitrary i,j∈I, F002 gives binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ-i)QY_(λ-j)=E_(iλ)E_(λj)=E_ij, as can also be checked on every basis vector. Substituting Q=Y_λ X_λ yields the asserted identity. Each factor preserves M_R by F001, and the scalar inverse belongs to R by F002; hence every E_ij preserves M_R. No comparison of weights modulo p is used.

By H001, 0∈I and n>0. Use the injection and identification in N002. For each i∈I, E_ii maps M_R onto J_i e_i: its image is contained there by coordinate projection, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. This image is finitely generated because the images of the n members of an R-basis of M_R generate it. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication by e_i identifies J_i with J_i e_i, so J_i is finitely generated. If c∈J_j, then c e_j∈M_R and E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i∈M_R by N002; hence J_j⊆J_i. Reversing i,j proves equality, and each equals J_0=J. At least one coordinate image is nonzero, since otherwise M_R would be zero, contradicting that its complex span is the nonzero V with n>0. Thus the common J is nonzero.

Each vector of M_R is the sum of its coordinate projections E_ii, so F001 places it in Σ_{i∈I}J e_i. Conversely each of these coordinate submodules is contained in M_R by definition. The sum is direct because (e_i) is a complex basis by N001: a relation Σc_i e_i=0 with c_i∈J⊆C forces every coefficient to vanish. Thus the coordinate-sum map J^I→M_R is an R-linear bijection, with inverse given by its coordinates. N001 supplies n>0 and the basis of V, and N002 supplies injectivity, rank n and complex spanning, giving all the other exported clauses.

By N003, J⊆C is finitely generated and nonzero, and M_R is free of rank n with coordinate decomposition J^I. Define T=Q⊗_R J and θ(q⊗c)=qc. The fraction field of R is Q: integers lie in R and every rational is a quotient of two elements of R with nonzero denominator. To see the multiplication map is injective, write any finite tensor sum over a common nonzero denominator s∈R as (1/s)⊗c with c∈J. If θ sends it to zero then c/s=0 in C, so c=0, and the tensor is zero. This also gives the usual identification of this tensor product with the localization of J. A finite R-generating family of J yields a finite Q-spanning family of T by tensoring; consequently T is finite dimensional. This proves the localization injectivity used here without presuming that containment J⊆C implies rank one.

Set r=dim_Q T. Tensor the R-coordinate isomorphism in N003 with Q. The result is a Q-linear isomorphism Q⊗_R M_R≅T^I: tensor the coordinate maps in each direction, and identify Q⊗_R J^I with T^I by q⊗(c_i)_i↦(q⊗c_i)_i, whose inverse sums the tensors supported at one coordinate. Finite I makes these mutually inverse. An R-basis of M_R of n members, supplied by N003, extends to a Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; its coefficient maps extend and prove both spanning and independence. Its dimension is therefore n. Apply M001 to the finite product T^I over Q: F001 gives finite dimension, hence a finite basis and finite generation; Q has the strong rank condition by the usual finite independent-family bound. M001 gives dim_Q T^I=Σ_{i∈I}dim_Q T=nr, using |I|=n. Thus n=nr, so r=1 because n>0 by N003. By F001, θ identifies T with a one-dimensional rational subspace of C containing J. In particular, for any nonzero a∈J and any c∈J there is a unique q∈Q with c=qa.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a nonempty finite generating family g of nonzero elements of J using N003. By F002, write its members as g_j=q_j a with q_j∈Q×. For each such rational q_j, removing all powers of the prime p from its nonzero integer numerator and denominator gives q_j=p^{d_j}u_j, where d_j∈Z and both u_j and u_j^(-1) lie in R: neither the remaining numerator nor denominator is divisible by p. This is just finite factorization by repeated division of nonzero integers by p, and works for positive or negative exponents and signs. The resulting finite family of integer exponents is nonempty.

Let d be the family of exponents from F003 and set u_j=p^(-d_j)q_j, a unit of R for each index j. Let ν=min_j d_j and define b=p^ν a. Since p is prime and a≠0, b≠0. For every generator q_j a, its ratio to b is p^{d_j-ν}u_j∈R because d_j≥ν. Thus J⊆Rb. For an index attaining the minimum, q_j a=u_j b and u_j is a unit, so b=u_j^(-1)q_j a∈J. Hence Rb⊆J and J=Rb. Finally the decomposition M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i from N003 becomes M_R=⊕_{i∈I}R b e_i. These vectors span, and are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex independent. They therefore form an R-basis. Export only existence of such b, discharging the private choices a,g,q and their identities.

Every integer denominator of an element of R is prime to p, so its image in the characteristic-p field K is nonzero by H001. Thus ρ:R→K, ρ(a/b)=ā b̄^(-1), is a well-defined ring map; equality of fractions and the ring laws follow by cross multiplication. Its kernel is pR and its residue field is Z/pZ: ρ(a/b)=0 exactly when p divides a. Define φ: M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse takes (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Both maps respect all tensor balancing relations and are inverse on pure tensors, which span. Also η:z⊗c↦(z mod pM_R)⊗c identifies M_R⊗_R K with (M_R/pM_R)⊗_(Z/pZ)K. The inverse sends (z mod pM_R)⊗c to z⊗c; changing z by p times a vector gives zero because pK=0, and all remaining balancing relations follow from ρ. These are the two natural isomorphisms of the supplied proof. H005 gives xM,yM⊆M and H003 gives h=xy-yx, hence hM⊆M. Tensoring these lattice operators commutes with φ and η by their formulas. The induced h equals h_K=x_Ky_K-y_Kx_K. The induced brackets therefore give the L_K-action, including characteristic 2.

Choose b from N004 and define B_i=φ^(-1)((b e_i)⊗1). The R-coordinate isomorphism M_R≅R^I given by the basis (b e_i) tensors to K^I; tensoring its coordinate maps gives inverse coefficient maps, proving that B is a K-basis, not merely a spanning family. Alternatively its reduction is a basis of M_R/pM_R over Z/pZ and then extends to K, via F001. N001 gives the matrices of x,y,h on e_i, and complex linearity gives the same matrices on b e_i. Their coefficients are integers, so extension along ρ and transport by φ give exactly x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for i≥1, y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for i<λ, y_K B_λ=0, and h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i, with integer coefficients read in K. Also n>0 by N001.

For every r with 0≤r≤λ<p, none of 1,...,r is divisible by p, so r! is nonzero in K by H001. Define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. On M the identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold; all these operators preserve M by H005. After extension they show that the induced X_r,Y_r are exactly A_r,C_r. For i,j∈I, N002 expresses E_ij as a composition of R-lattice operators and the unit binom(λ,j)^(-1). Its extension, transported by φ, sends B_j to B_i and every other B-coordinate to zero, hence is the map T_ij defined from F002. The image of that unit under ρ remains a unit and is the inverse of the coefficient binom(λ,j) in K, so this coefficient is nonzero. Substituting the just established induced divided powers in N002 gives T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). This proves every exported clause of the output without comparing reduced weights.

By N005 choose B and its matrix units T. There are n=λ+1>0 basis vectors, so V_K≠0. Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. Invariance under x_K and y_K implies invariance under their nonnegative powers and scalar multiples, so under every A_r,C_r in N005. Composing these operators and multiplying by binom(λ,j)^(-1) shows, using the N005 identity, that every T_ij preserves W. This assertion holds for all i,j∈I. By classical cases W=0 or W≠0. Under the zero branch L3: W=0, the desired disjunction holds immediately, and L3 is discharged. In the remaining branch assume L2: W≠0; then there exists a nonzero vector of W.
Choose 0≠w∈W using F001 and expand w=Σ_{i∈I}c_i B_i in the basis N005. If every c_i were zero then the expansion would give w=0, a contradiction. Thus there exists an index j∈I with c_j≠0.

Choose such j by F002. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit definition gives T_ij w=c_j B_i. By F001 this vector is in W, and c_j is invertible in the field K. Hence B_i=c_j^(-1)T_ij w∈W. All basis vectors belong to W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 and combine with the zero branch to obtain W=0 or W=V_K under L1. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. By N005 the operators are the induced lattice actions, and by H003 the integer span of x,y,h is closed under bracket; the induced action is the stated L_K-action. Its invariant subspaces are exactly the subspaces invariant under these three generators. H005 ensures these are the actions on the original arbitrary lattice tensor product V_K. Finally H001 permits λ=0 (all factorials and binomial coefficients used equal one) and permits p=2 with λ=0 or 1. None of the argument required distinct h_K eigenvalues or algebraic closure of K. This proves P in the full original domain.

roots.statement: p is a prime integer, K is a field of characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight λ and of complex dimension λ+1.
The Chevalley generators satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h, both in sl2(C) and in the action on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊆V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No equality with the minimal lattice is assumed.

Let A be any semiring satisfying the strong rank condition (every injective A-linear map A^s→A^t between finite free modules forces s≤t). Let T be a finite indexing type, and let F_t, t∈T, be additive commutative monoids with A-module structures, each free and finitely generated over A. Then Module.finrank_A(∏_{t∈T}F_t)=Σ_{t∈T}Module.finrank_A(F_t), where finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (and agrees with finite vector-space dimension over a field).

hypotheses: A is a semiring satisfying the strong rank condition.
For every t∈T, F_t is an additive commutative monoid with an A-module structure.
Every F_t is a free A-module.
Every F_t is a finitely generated A-module.

For i∈I: xe_0=0; xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) if i≥1; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) if i<λ and ye_λ=0; he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all i,j∈I the integer binom(λ,j) is a unit of R and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ-i) Y_λ X_λ Y_(λ-j). In particular every E_ij preserves M_R.
source_outputs.N003: n>0, (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V, μ is injective, and the identified M_R⊆V is free of rank n over R and spans V over C. For every i∈I, J_i=J. The R-submodule J⊆C is finitely generated and nonzero, and M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i inside V; explicitly the map (c_i)_{i∈I}↦Σ_{i∈I}c_i e_i is an R-linear isomorphism from the finite product J^I to M_R.
source_outputs.N004: There exists a nonzero complex number b∈J such that J=Rb and (b e_i)_{i∈I}, viewed in M_R through the injective map μ, is an R-basis of M_R.
source_outputs.N005: n>0 and there exists a K-basis B=(B_i)_{i∈I} of V_K. On this basis x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for 1≤i≤λ; y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ and y_K B_λ=0; h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i. These are exactly the induced actions of x,y,h, so they define the stated L_K-action. All integer coefficients here are mapped into K. For 0≤r≤λ, r! is nonzero in K; define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. For i,j∈I let T_ij be the K-linear map B_j↦B_i with all other basis vectors mapped to zero. Then binom(λ,j) is nonzero in K and T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). Moreover A_r,C_r are precisely the induced divided powers X_r,Y_r on V_K.
source_outputs.P: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L_K-module, for every field K of characteristic p and every integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

result.text:
1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183: 
184: ## Input status
185: 
186: This file fixes the exercise, notation and supplied proof, including the
187: arbitrary-lattice argument. It is not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
188: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must construct and check
189: those artifacts from these explicit inputs, registering any foundational
190: module or localization results used by their NL0.

value.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L_K-module, for every field K of characteristic p and every integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 300-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and independent endpoint-fidelity Audit B remain required.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.

51: /-- Lift an `R`-balanced map to the tensor product.
52: A map `f : M →+ N →+ P` additive in both components is `R`-balanced, or middle linear with respect
53: to `R`, if scalar multiplication in either argument is equivalent, `f (r • m) n = f m (r • n)`.
54: Note that strictly the first action should be a right-action by `R`, but for now `R` is commutative
55: so it doesn't matter. -/
56: -- TODO: use this to implement `lift` and `SMul.aux`. For now we do not do this as it causes
57: -- performance issues elsewhere.
58: def liftAddHom (f : M →+ N →+ P)
59:     (hf : ∀ (r : R) (m : M) (n : N), f (r • m) n = f m (r • n)) :
60:     M ⊗[R] N →+ P :=
61:   (addConGen (TensorProduct.Eqv R M N)).lift (FreeAddMonoid.lift (fun mn : M × N => f mn.1 mn.2)) <|
62:     AddCon.addConGen_le.2 fun x y hxy =>
63:       match x, y, hxy with
64:       | _, _, .of_zero_left n =>
65:         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_zero, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, map_zero,
66:           AddMonoidHom.zero_apply]
67:       | _, _, .of_zero_right m =>
68:         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_zero, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, map_zero]
69:       | _, _, .of_add_left m₁ m₂ n =>
70:         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, map_add,
71:           AddMonoidHom.add_apply]
72:       | _, _, .of_add_right m n₁ n₂ =>
73:         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, map_add]
74:       | _, _, .of_smul s m n =>
75:         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by rw [FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, hf]
76:       | _, _, .add_comm x y =>
77:         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, add_comm]
78: 
79: @[simp]
80: theorem liftAddHom_tmul (f : M →+ N →+ P)
81:     (hf : ∀ (r : R) (m : M) (n : N), f (r • m) n = f m (r • n)) (m : M) (n : N) :
82:     liftAddHom f hf (m ⊗ₜ n) = f m n :=
83:   rfl

21: 
22: - `Algebra.TensorProduct.semiring`: the ring structure on `A ⊗[R] B` for two `R`-algebras `A`, `B`.
23: - `Algebra.TensorProduct.leftAlgebra`: the `S`-algebra structure on `A ⊗[R] B`, for when `A` is
24:   additionally an `S` algebra.

43: section liftBaseChange
44: 
45: variable {R M N} (A) [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] [AddCommMonoid M]
46: variable [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module A N] [IsScalarTower R A N]
47: 
48: /--
49: If `M` is an `R`-module and `N` is an `A`-module, then `A`-linear maps `A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N`
50: correspond to `R` linear maps `M →ₗ[R] N` by composing with `M → A ⊗ M`, `x ↦ 1 ⊗ x`.
51: -/
52: def liftBaseChangeEquiv : (M →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[A] (A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N) :=
53:   (LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf _ _ _).symm.trans (AlgebraTensorModule.lift.equiv _ _ _ _ _ _)
54: 
55: /-- If `N` is an `A` module, we may lift a linear map `M →ₗ[R] N` to `A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N` -/
56: abbrev liftBaseChange (l : M →ₗ[R] N) : A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N :=
57:   LinearMap.liftBaseChangeEquiv A l
58: 
59: @[simp]
60: lemma liftBaseChange_tmul (l : M →ₗ[R] N) (x y) : l.liftBaseChange A (x ⊗ₜ y) = x • l y := rfl
61: 
62: lemma liftBaseChange_one_tmul (l : M →ₗ[R] N) (y) : l.liftBaseChange A (1 ⊗ₜ y) = l y := by simp
63: 
64: @[simp]
65: lemma liftBaseChangeEquiv_symm_apply (l : A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] N) (x) :
66:     (liftBaseChangeEquiv A).symm l x = l (1 ⊗ₜ x) := rfl
67: 
68: lemma liftBaseChange_comp {P} [AddCommMonoid P] [Module A P] [Module R P] [IsScalarTower R A P]
69:     (l : M →ₗ[R] N) (l' : N →ₗ[A] P) :
70:       l' ∘ₗ l.liftBaseChange A = (l'.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ l).liftBaseChange A := by
71:   ext
72:   simp
73: 
74: @[simp]
75: lemma range_liftBaseChange (l : M →ₗ[R] N) :
76:     LinearMap.range (l.liftBaseChange A) = Submodule.span A (LinearMap.range l) := by
77:   apply le_antisymm
78:   · rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
79:     induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on
80:     · simp
81:     · rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul]
82:       exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨_, rfl⟩)
83:     · rw [map_add]
84:       exact add_mem ‹_› ‹_›
85:   · rw [Submodule.span_le]
86:     rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
87:     exact ⟨1 ⊗ₜ x, by simp⟩
88: 
89: end liftBaseChange
90: 
91: end LinearMap

1: # Accepted NL0 revision, frozen translation and Audit B
2: 
3: This is the execution guide for Yui's translation stage. Preserve the accepted
4: original NL0/Audit A. The runtime adapters compose their existing checks;
5: Python handles exact edits, versions, scheduling and evidence. Models/humans
6: still inspect mathematics, choose Lean representations and author local plans.
7: Automatic semantic compilation of arbitrary papers is not claimed.
8: 
9: ## 1. Inspect before extracting
10: 
11: ```sh
12: python3 scripts/source_preparation.py inventory \
13:   --graph /absolute/original/nl0.json --spec /absolute/original/spec.json \
14:   --audit-a /absolute/original/audit-a.json
15: ```
16: 
17: The result contains canonical direct consumers and exact paragraph hashes/text.
18: Start from existing exports. Inspect repeated derivations and their scopes;
19: do not ask a model to reprove or rewrite every node. Zero useful candidates is
20: valid: keep the accepted original and skip revision entirely. Fanout is not
21: avoided proof cost. Tiny helpers may cost more to discover/review than they save.
22: 
23: Models may propose candidates; select only existing derivations with a clear
24: closed interface. No automatic optimal selection or exhaustive discovery is
25: promised. Keep discovery, selection and owner intervention visible in costs.
26: 
27: ## 2. Stage a bounded patch
28: 
29: `patch.json` has `version: "nl0-local-revision-1"`, `baseline_graph_sha256`,
30: `spec_sha256`, optional `discovery_and_author_cost_seconds` and `candidates`.
31: Each candidate has exactly:
32: 
33: - `id`, `proposition`: one complete new internal N record;
34: - `producer`: one complete new R record under the parent current-v2 schema;
35: - `derivation`: `{inference: R_ID, paragraphs: [S_ID, ...]}` pointing to the
36:   already supplied derivation;
37: - Put the baseline revision/old R/S and current producer separately in the new
38:   proposition's origin. Historical provenance is not a current dependency edge.
39: - `expected_avoided_work`: a concrete basis, with unmeasured assumptions disclosed;
40: - `consumers`: at least two distinct actual consumer records.
41: 
42: Each consumer has `inference`, `before_sha256` (the canonical sorted JSON hash
43: of the old R), `inputs`, `replacements`, optional retained `applications`, and
44: `cut`. The direct inputs may retain/remove old ones and add only this new N.
45: Each replacement gives the stable `paragraph`, `before_sha256` of its full old
46: paragraph, and preferably `splices: [{old, new}, ...]` plus `uses_after`.
47: Every old string must match once, with no overlapping spans. Unselected text
48: is preserved byte for byte. Optional `uses_local_after`/`objects_after` adjust
49: the explicit accounting. A complete `after` paragraph is also supported for
50: small paragraphs, but cannot change local fact records or assumption lifetimes.
51: 
52: `cut` gives `old_conclusion`, `shared_instantiation`, `supplied_conclusion`,
53: `conditions: [{condition, justification}, ...]`, and `continuation`. Spell out
54: bindings, domains, exceptional sets/representatives and every fact/object the
55: untouched continuation needs. A new citation alone is not substitution.
56: 
57: Do not change original H/E/M/D, logic, target, old proposition statements, or
58: unrelated arguments. The adapter rejects overlapping consumer patches, added
59: consumer source applications and changed local-fact/assumption lifetimes.
60: Defer unsupported edits instead of expanding to a full proof rewrite.
61: 
62: ```sh
63: python3 scripts/source_preparation.py stage \
64:   --graph /absolute/original/nl0.json --spec /absolute/original/spec.json \
65:   --audit-a /absolute/original/audit-a.json \
66:   --patch /absolute/patch.json --out /absolute/new-revision
67: ```
68: 
69: The output contains unchanged-spec `case/spec.json`, revised `case/nl0.json`,
70: exact source dependencies, producer/cut packets, pending review templates,
71: patch and binding manifest. Never overwrite an accepted stage. A later revision
72: may supply `--incremental /absolute/previous/source-acceptance.json` instead of
73: ordinary `--audit-a`; the adapter revalidates its chain and rejects cycles.
74: 
75: ## 3. Complete actual scoped reviews and accept the revised source
76: 
77: Fill `case/producer-review.json` only from actual fresh reviews of each complete
78: producer packet. It uses ordinary parent Audit A entries, including checks,
79: located evidence, source applications and exact fresh-packet replay boundaries.
80: The producer-only reviewer need not establish the old derivation's provenance
81: or whole-graph acceptance from a packet that lacks those materials.
82: 
83: Fill `case/cut-review.json` from the paired cut packets. Its checks are
84: `existing_derivation`, `condition_discharge`, `conclusion_match`,
85: `continuation_preservation`, `dependency_accounting`. Require an actual verdict,
86: specific notes, evidence and the paired `/before`, `/after`, `/contract`,
87: `/old_derivation`, `/producer_source_derivation`, `/shared_statement`, `/input_statements_before`,
88: `/input_statements_after`, `/global_context` locations. Evidence paths are relative
89: to `case/`, as in the parent checker. This is delta review with baseline access,
90: not a new independent fresh replay of the whole consumer. E/M applications
91: retain the parent schema; N uses belong in inputs/citations/explicit prose.
92: `old_derivation` is this consumer's actual replaced baseline proof.
93: `producer_source_derivation` is the one selected original proof of the shared
94: intermediate result, which may come from another consumer. Different final
95: consumer goals are expected; compare the shared intermediate conclusion instead.
96: Keep each generated `packet_sha256`: a review from a different cut packet cannot
97: be reused merely because IDs and pointer names coincide. Exact reuse after
98: record-only changes requires byte-identical source and actual reviewed packets,
99: with original verdicts, evidence, carrier and acquisition cost retained.
100: 
101: ```sh
102: python3 scripts/source_preparation.py check --out /absolute/new-revision
103: ```
104: 
105: This writes `source-acceptance.json`. It retains original audit qualifications,
106: records new-full/substitution/inherited coverage and invokes the parent rules
107: for new producers. Unchanged consumers/downstream conditional arguments need
108: no new mathematical replay when their inputs, context and conventions remain
109: unchanged. Python still rechecks the graph and exact preserved bytes.
110: 
111: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires an accepted current-v2 baseline and every
112: actual local review. A missing/unverified baseline yields development-only local
113: review and cannot enter the complete production gate. No new receipt falsely
114: claims the parent issued a fresh whole-graph audit-v3 pass. Hashes do not prove
115: mathematical correctness or authenticate a reviewer who fabricates judgment.
116: 
117: ## 4. Author and freeze the IR
118: 
119: Choose object views, input/output types, planned typed conversion interfaces, shared
120: ports and local T plans jointly. Preserve natural NL0 node boundaries. Export
121: every fact needed by another task; no shared result is an ambient definition.
122: The source graph is now fixed. Representation/API difficulties remain Lean
123: engineering; substantive source changes require a separately reviewed revision.
124: 
125: For the whole workflow the contract's relative `source.path` points to exact
126: canonical NL0 bytes, not a summary. `source_steps` copy every argument paragraph
127: with distinct implementation IDs. The controller copies these paragraphs and
128: note locations from the accepted source rather than asking the author to
129: transcribe them. The author supplies types and local plans, and can save partial
130: JSON before completing the whole interface.
131: 
132: The lower-level mechanical freeze uses a checked binding with
133: `source_graph_sha256`, `contract_sha256`, `plan_sha256`, `paragraph_mapping` and
134: `source_outputs`. It checks exact source coverage and direct boundaries and runs
135: Lean type elaboration. This binding is **not a semantic review receipt**; the
136: recorded semantic status is `PENDING_AUDIT_B`. This legacy route requires explicit semantic review before claiming complete
137: acceptance. Normal full/translation entry runs the independent interface reviewer
138: and reads back its actual hash-bound PASS before freezing/dispatch; final machine
139: Audit B inherits it only after actual full endpoint and proof-integrity checks. The commands below expose the
140: lower-level compatibility path; use `--interface-review` to supply an actual
141: review when constructing a workflow manually. See [repair routing](proof-repair.md).
142: 
143: ```sh
144: python3 scripts/workflow.py freeze /absolute/new-workflow \
145:   --graph /absolute/new-revision/case/nl0.json \
146:   --spec /absolute/new-revision/case/spec.json \
147:   --incremental /absolute/new-revision/source-acceptance.json \
148:   --contract /absolute/interface/contract.json --plan /absolute/interface/plan.json \
149:   --interface-binding /absolute/interface/accepted-interface-paths.json \
150:   --max-concurrency auto
151: ```
152: 
153: Without extraction use original graph/spec and ordinary `--audit-a`. Freeze
154: binds original/revised source, evidence, IR, mechanical binding (or optional review), source paragraphs and code.
155: Any later change blocks the next stage. It does not regenerate old task packets
156: or automatically rerun mathematical audits.
157: `freeze-seal.json` binds the complete run manifest, including configuration and
158: source-output mapping. Editing that manifest invalidates the gate. This is
159: integrity bookkeeping, not authentication of an owner who rewrites every record.
160: 
161: ## 5. Run bounded proof work and actual assembly
162: 
163: Follow [the execution protocol](execution-protocol.md) for queue ownership,
164: per-case budgets, structured status, cancellation and finite batch exit.
165: 
166: ```sh
167: python3 scripts/workflow.py run /absolute/new-workflow \
168:   --shared-store /absolute/project/shared-store --timeout-seconds 180
169: ```
170: 
171: The workflow's concurrency is fixed at freeze: `auto` uses a confirmed backend
172: cap when available, otherwise the CLI's disclosed fallback two. A positive N is
173: user-controlled, constrained only by a known backend hard limit. Print requested,
174: effective and reason; record observed peak, per-stage queue/start/end and total
175: time. The proof budget covers proof jobs, retries and their optional diagnostics;
176: translation preparation and Audit B use a separate serial lane. Earlier
177: local Audit A R reviews have a separate N-slot lane. One case ledger includes
178: all phases. This is not account-wide distributed rate control.
179: Other cases own separate budgets. Python coordination consumes no model slot.
180: Free slots take the next queued node; own revisions retain that node's conversation.
181: 
182: Proof workers see only their frozen ports, allowed statements, own NL paragraphs
183: and relevant definitions/views. No sibling proof or reference answer is sent.
184: Shared source lookup is exact, rechecked by Lean, and a miss launches ordinary
185: proof work. Shared production and conditional consumers may run concurrently;
186: actual assembly closes every dependency. Failure leaves the root unfinished.
187: 
188: `run_graph.py --max-concurrency auto|N` remains a frozen-port-only command;
189: `model_pilot.py` provides the internal isolated proof stage. Neither alone
190: claims whole-proof Audit B. Integer `--workers` / `--max-model-stages` remain
191: compatibility aliases, with conflicts rejected.
192: 
193: ## 6. Execute Audit B and finish
194: 
195: After all local jobs pass, first attempt mechanical assembly under
196: [the assembly protocol](assembly.md). The serial connection author repairs only
197: actual connection/library-discharge issues and internal bodies under unchanged
198: frozen E/P and meaning-determining definitions.

200: For a workflow with a genuine passing `--interface-review` receipt:
201: 
202: ```sh
203: python3 scripts/workflow.py audit-prepare /absolute/new-workflow
204: python3 scripts/workflow.py audit-build /absolute/new-workflow
205: python3 scripts/workflow.py audit-check /absolute/new-workflow --machine
206: ```
207: 
208: Normal `yui.py run --track full|translate` performs this sequence, verifies actual
209: frozen full E/P and complete standalone dependencies/trust, and inherits the
210: pre-proof semantic authority. It dispatches no final semantic LLM.
211: 
212: Only proof-integrity success with genuine E/P/meaning drift opens B-final.
213: Faithful drift is warning-qualified with a freeze-defect report; nonfaithful or
214: unverified output pauses for an explicit `final-decision` command. Source warnings
215: never become ordinary PASS. Invalid compilation, `sorry`, dependency failure or
216: changed provenance cannot be overridden by a semantic review.
217: 
218: The lower-level legacy/manual path remains available through
219: `audit-check --review /absolute/completed-review.json`. It requires an actual
220: located review under its historical schema. A pending template never passes,
221: and it does not acquire a pre-proof semantic history by being compiled.

224: attempts and distinguish model-budget exhaustion from execution faults. Final
225: reports separate preparation, freeze, proof makespan, queued/model-stage costs,
226: assembly and audit; uninstrumented owner work stays UNMEASURED. Cold and warm
227: reuse costs are separate, first construction is not free, and nested tool time

def image (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  LinearMap.range (mu p M)
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=

def unit {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    {n : ℕ} (B : Module.Basis (Fin n) F W) (i j : Fin n) : Module.End F W :=

def at {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    {n : ℕ} (B : Module.Basis (Fin n) F W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
  if hi : i < n then B ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
end LatticeIR

47:     (hsmul : ∀ (c) (x : M), f c • x = c • x) : Module S M :=
48:   { hf.distribMulActionLeft f.toMonoidHom hsmul with
49:     zero_smul := fun x => by rw [← f.map_zero, hsmul, zero_smul]

50: /-- If we put an `R`-algebra structure on a semiring `S`, we get a natural equivalence from the
51: category of `S`-modules to the category of representations of the algebra `S` (over `R`). The type
52: synonym `RestrictScalars` is essentially this equivalence.
53: 
54: Warning: use this type synonym judiciously! Consider an example where we want to construct an
55: `R`-linear map from `M` to `S`, given:
56: ```lean
57: variable (R S M : Type*)
58: variable [CommSemiring R] [Semiring S] [Algebra R S] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module S M]
59: ```
60: With the assumptions above we can't directly state our map as we have no `Module R M` structure, but
61: `RestrictScalars` permits it to be written as:
62: ```lean
63: -- an `R`-module structure on `M` is provided by `RestrictScalars` which is compatible
64: example : RestrictScalars R S M →ₗ[R] S := sorry
65: ```
66: However, it is usually better just to add this extra structure as an argument:
67: ```lean
68: -- an `R`-module structure on `M` and proof of its compatibility is provided by the user
69: example [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M] : M →ₗ[R] S := sorry
70: ```
71: The advantage of the second approach is that it defers the duty of providing the missing typeclasses
72: `[Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]`. If some concrete `M` naturally carries these (as is often
73: the case) then we have avoided `RestrictScalars` entirely. If not, we can pass
74: `RestrictScalars R S M` later on instead of `M`.
75: 
76: Note that this means we almost always want to state definitions and lemmas in the language of
77: `IsScalarTower` rather than `RestrictScalars`.
78: 
79: An example of when one might want to use `RestrictScalars` would be if one has a vector space
80: over a field of characteristic zero and wishes to make use of the `ℚ`-algebra structure. -/

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace LatticeIR
def R (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
instance ratModule (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module ℚ V :=
  Module.compHom V (algebraMap ℚ ℂ)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (R p).subtype).toAlgebra
instance localModule (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V :=
  Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
def dp (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := dp y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := (R p) ⊗[ℤ] M
def mu (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def image (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  LinearMap.range (mu p M)
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
  letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ ℂ := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ ℂ
  (image p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def unit {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    {n : ℕ} (B : Module.Basis (Fin n) F W) (i j : Fin n) : Module.End F W :=
  (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton F W (B i)).comp (B.coord j)
def basisAt {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    {n : ℕ} (B : Module.Basis (Fin n) F W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
  if hi : i < n then B ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def Stable (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ M, f w ∈ M
def latticeOp (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  letI := Classical.propDecidable
  if hf : Stable M f then (f.restrictScalars ℤ).restrict hf else 0
def kop (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End K (VK K M) :=
  (latticeOp M f).baseChange K
def kdp {K W : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W]
    (f : Module.End K W) (r : ℕ) : Module.End K W :=
  ((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def Coordinates (lam : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) ℂ V, ∀ i, B i = e y v i.val
def rop (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End (R p) (MR p M) :=
  (latticeOp M f).baseChange (R p)
def Inv {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    (W' : Submodule F W) (f : Module.End F W) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W', f w ∈ W'
def Actions {F W : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    (lam : ℤ) (a b c : Module.End F W) (B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) F W) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, a (B i) = if i.val = 0 then 0 else
    ((lam - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • basisAt B (i.val - 1)) ∧
  (∀ i, b (B i) = if i.val < lam.toNat then
    ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • basisAt B (i.val + 1) else 0) ∧
  (∀ i, c (B i) = ((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • B i)
def Strings (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ d : ℕ, h ((y ^ d) v) = ((lam - 2 * (d : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ d) v) ∧
  (∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → x ((y ^ d) v) =
    (((d : ℤ) * (lam - (d : ℤ) + 1) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ (d - 1)) v)
def ComplexOutput (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  0 < lam + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
  Coordinates lam y v ∧ Strings lam x y h v ∧
  (∀ d : ℕ, lam < (d : ℤ) → (y ^ d) v = 0) ∧
  (∀ B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) ℂ V,
    (∀ i, B i = e y v i.val) → Actions lam x y h B) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Fin (lam.toNat + 1)),
    dp x r (e y v i.val) =
      if r ≤ i.val then ((Nat.choose (lam.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℕ) : ℂ) • e y v (i.val - r) else 0) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Fin (lam.toNat + 1)),
    dp y r (e y v i.val) =
      if i.val + r ≤ lam.toNat then ((Nat.choose (i.val + r) r : ℕ) : ℂ) • e y v (i.val + r) else 0)
def LocalBasics (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (mu p M) ∧
  Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) (R p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (image p M : Set V) = ⊤ ∧
  (∀ r : ℕ, (∀ z, mu p M (rop p M (dp x r) z) = dp x r (mu p M z)) ∧
    (∀ z, mu p M (rop p M (dp y r) z) = dp y r (mu p M z))) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (w : V), w ∈ image p M → dp x r w ∈ image p M ∧ dp y r w ∈ image p M)
def MatrixOutput (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  LocalBasics p lam M x y ∧
  (∀ j : Fin (lam.toNat + 1), IsUnit (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : R p)) ∧
  (∀ B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) ℂ V,
    (∀ i, B i = e y v i.val) → ∀ i j,
    unit B i j =
      ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℂ)⁻¹) •
      (dp x (lam.toNat - i.val) * dp y lam.toNat * dp x lam.toNat * dp y (lam.toNat - j.val)) ∧
    ∀ w ∈ image p M, unit B i j w ∈ image p M)
def CommonOutput (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  0 < lam + 1 ∧ Coordinates lam y v ∧ LocalBasics p lam M x y ∧
  (∀ i : Fin (lam.toNat + 1), Ji p M y v i.val = Ji p M y v 0) ∧
  (Ji p M y v 0).FG ∧ Ji p M y v 0 ≠ ⊥ ∧
  (∃ F : ((Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) → Ji p M y v 0) ≃ₗ[R p] MR p M,
    ∀ c, mu p M (F c) = ∑ i, ((c i : Ji p M y v 0) : ℂ) • e y v i.val)
def PrincipalOutput (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℂ, b ∈ Ji p M y v 0 ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧
    Ji p M y v 0 = Submodule.span (R p) {b} ∧
    ∃ B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) (R p) (MR p M),
      ∀ i, mu p M (B i) = b • e y v i.val
def ReducedOutput (K : Type*) [Field K] (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  0 < lam + 1 ∧ Stable M x ∧ Stable M y ∧ Stable M h ∧
  kop K M h = kop K M x * kop K M y - kop K M y * kop K M x ∧
  kop K M h * kop K M x - kop K M x * kop K M h = (2 : K) • kop K M x ∧
  kop K M h * kop K M y - kop K M y * kop K M h = (-2 : K) • kop K M y ∧
  ∃ B : Module.Basis (Fin (lam.toNat + 1)) K (VK K M),
    Actions lam (kop K M x) (kop K M y) (kop K M h) B ∧
    (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat → (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧
      (latticeOp M (dp x r)).baseChange K = kdp (kop K M x) r ∧
      (latticeOp M (dp y r)).baseChange K = kdp (kop K M y) r) ∧
    (∀ i j : Fin (lam.toNat + 1), (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
      unit B i j = ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : K)⁻¹) •
        (kdp (kop K M x) (lam.toNat - i.val) * kdp (kop K M y) lam.toNat *
         kdp (kop K M x) lam.toNat * kdp (kop K M y) (lam.toNat - j.val)))
def Target (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧ ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
    Inv W (kop K M x) → Inv W (kop K M y) → Inv W (kop K M h) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
end LatticeIR
open LatticeIR
types: ComplexOutput lam x y h v
MatrixOutput p lam M x y v
CommonOutput p lam M x y v
PrincipalOutput p lam M y v
ReducedOutput K lam M x y h
Target K M x y h
